notes: Read all 76 source lines before editing. useInView is built on the browser IntersectionObserver, which React Native does not provide; per contract rules 4 & 7 the port is a native-safe implementation with an explicit unavailable state that reuses the web hook's OWN documented SSR/jsdom fallback (report inView=true immediately), so no DOM/Recharts/Leaflet/web-UI module is imported.

L1-18 the doc block (purpose, lazy-mount/animation use cases, the freezeOnceVisible latch behavior, and the explicit SSR-safe 'IntersectionObserver undefined -> report true immediately' contract) is ported and expanded into the file header so the web semantics + the native unavailable-state mapping are both documented.

L20 `import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type RefObject } from 'react'` -> retained `useRef`, `useState`, `type RefObject`; `useEffect` is dropped because its sole purpose was to create/configure the IntersectionObserver, which never exists on native (kept only the imports actually used to avoid an unused-import lint error). Added `import React` (for the `React.ComponentRef` host-node type, mirroring the proven SkipToContent.tsx native pattern) and `import { type View } from 'react-native'` for `typeof View`.

L22-31 `UseInViewOptions` interface ported with all four fields and their JSDoc/defaults verbatim: rootMargin?: string (L23-24), threshold?: number | number[] (L25-26), and freezeOnceVisible?: boolean (L29-30) are byte-identical. The DOM `root?: Element | null` (L27-28) is retyped to its native host-node analog `React.ComponentRef<typeof View> | null` (no `Element` type on native) with the 'Optional scroll root' JSDoc preserved. All four remain part of the public API for source compatibility; without an observer they are inert and documented as such.

L33-35 the signature `useInView<T extends Element = HTMLDivElement>(options = {}): { ref: RefObject<T>; inView: boolean }` is ported: the DOM-typed generic `T extends Element = HTMLDivElement` becomes `T = React.ComponentRef<typeof View>` (native View host node is the analog of an HTMLDivElement, and there is no `Element` base to constrain against on native). Return shape `{ ref; inView }` is unchanged; `RefObject<T>` is written `RefObject<T | null>` purely because React 19's `useRef<T>(null)` overload returns `RefObject<T | null>` (verified in @types/react index.d.ts L1749) — the same `{ current: T | null }` that the web's React 18 `RefObject<T>` denoted, so the runtime contract is identical.

L36-41 the `options` destructuring with defaults (rootMargin='200px', threshold=0, root=null, freezeOnceVisible=true) is intentionally not reproduced because on native the values can never reach an observer; the defaults are preserved in the L22-31 interface JSDoc instead, and the parameter is named `_options` so @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars (error, argsIgnorePattern '^_') passes. (Re-adding a parity-only `useEffect` with the web's `[rootMargin, threshold, root, freezeOnceVisible]` deps array would fail the repo's react-hooks/exhaustive-deps rule, which is severity 2/error here, as unnecessary dependencies — so the honest native form omits it.)
L43 `const ref = useRef<T>(null)` ported verbatim — the ref the caller attaches to its target is unchanged.

L44-46 `const [inView, setInView] = useState<boolean>(() => typeof IntersectionObserver === 'undefined')` ported as `const [inView] = useState<boolean>(() => !intersectionObserverAvailable)`: the SSR-detection lazy initializer is preserved 1:1 in meaning. `intersectionObserverAvailable` probes `(globalThis as { IntersectionObserver?: unknown }).IntersectionObserver` (the native-safe form of `typeof IntersectionObserver === 'undefined'`, matching the existing native `(globalThis as {...}).localStorage` style and needing no DOM lib types); it is always false on RN, so `inView` seeds to true. `setInView` is dropped from the tuple because, without an observer, nothing transitions the state — `inView` stays at its true seed, which IS the web's documented fallback value.
L47 `const seenRef = useRef(false)` is omitted: it exists only to remember a prior intersection for the freezeOnceVisible latch, which has no observer to drive it on native.

L49-73 the entire `useEffect` is omitted because it is the IntersectionObserver setup: L50-53 SSR fallback (setInView(true)) is already realized by seeding inView=true; L54-55 node guard, L56 seen/freeze guard, L58-70 `new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => { ... isIntersecting -> seen/setInView(true)/disconnect; else if !freezeOnceVisible -> setInView(false) }, { rootMargin, threshold, root })`, L71 observer.observe(node), and L72 cleanup `() => observer.disconnect()` all reference the browser-only IntersectionObserver constructor + DOM `entry.isIntersecting` and have no React Native analog (contract rules 4 & 7). L73 deps `[rootMargin, threshold, root, freezeOnceVisible]` is therefore not reproduced.
L75 `return { ref, inView }` ported verbatim — identical public return value (ref + boolean).

L76 closing brace preserved. No DOM-only modules, HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components are imported — only react + the react-native View type. Verified via: cd apps/native; npm run typecheck; npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
